evals.prompt:
I ran `npm audit --json` on our Express API and got this output. Which ones are urgent and what do I actually need to run?

```json
{
  "auditReportVersion": 2,
  "vulnerabilities": {
    "lodash": {
      "name": "lodash",
      "severity": "high",
      "isDirect": true,
      "via": [
        {
          "source": 1067960,
          "name": "lodash",
          "dependency": "lodash",
          "title": "Prototype Pollution in lodash",
          "url": "https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fvqr-27wr-82fm",
          "severity": "high",
          "cwe": ["CWE-1321"],
          "cvss": { "score": 7.4 },
          "range": "<4.17.21"
        }
      ],
      "fixAvailable": true,
      "range": "<4.17.21",
      "nodes": ["node_modules/lodash"]
    },
    "minimist": {
      "name": "minimist",
      "severity": "critical",
      "isDirect": false,
      "via": [
        {
          "source": 1068024,
          "name": "minimist",
          "dependency": "minimist",
          "title": "Prototype Pollution in minimist",
          "url": "https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h",
          "severity": "critical",
          "cwe": ["CWE-1321"],
          "cvss": { "score": 9.8 },
          "range": "<1.2.6"
        }
      ],
      "fixAvailable": { "name": "mkdirp", "version": "1.0.4", "isSemVerMajor": true },
      "range": "<1.2.6",
      "nodes": ["node_modules/mkdirp/node_modules/minimist"]
    },
    "ansi-regex": {
      "name": "ansi-regex",
      "severity": "moderate",
      "isDirect": false,
      "via": [
        {
          "source": 1067894,
          "name": "ansi-regex",
          "dependency": "ansi-regex",
          "title": "Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity in ansi-regex",
          "url": "https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-93q8-gq69-wqmw",
          "severity": "moderate",
          "cwe": ["CWE-1333"],
          "cvss": { "score": 5.3 },
          "range": ">2.1.1 <5.0.1 || >=6.0.0 <6.0.1"
        }
      ],
      "fixAvailable": true,
      "range": ">2.1.1 <5.0.1 || >=6.0.0 <6.0.1",
      "nodes": ["node_modules/ansi-regex"]
    }
  },
  "metadata": {
    "vulnerabilities": { "info": 0, "low": 0, "moderate": 1, "high": 1, "critical": 1, "total": 3 }
  }
}
```

We're running lodash 4.17.20, mkdirp 0.5.5 (which pulls in minimist 0.2.4), and have ansi-regex 3.0.0 as a transitive dep. What order should I fix these in and what commands do I run?
evals.expected_output: A prioritized fix plan: minimist (critical prototype pollution, CVSS 9.8) first — but since the fix requires a major bump in mkdirp (isSemVerMajor: true), should explain this needs `npm install mkdirp@latest` or deliberate use of `npm audit fix --force` after a dry-run preview. Then lodash (high, direct dep, fixAvailable: true) with `npm install lodash@latest` or `npm audit fix`. Then ansi-regex (moderate, transitive). Should include commands, explain the isSemVerMajor flag for minimist, and recommend re-running `npm audit` at the end.

assertions.name: minimist-identified-as-top-priority
assertions.description: minimist (or its parent mkdirp) is identified as the highest priority to fix due to critical severity / CVSS 9.8

assertions.name: correct-severity-ordering
assertions.description: lodash (high) is addressed before ansi-regex (moderate) in the fix order

assertions.name: issemvermajor-explained
assertions.description: The isSemVerMajor flag on the minimist fix is mentioned — explaining that the fix requires a breaking-change upgrade of mkdirp

assertions.name: fix-commands-provided
assertions.description: Specific npm commands are given for the affected packages (not just general advice)

assertions.name: re-audit-recommended
assertions.description: Recommends re-running `npm audit` after fixes to confirm all advisories are resolved

evals.prompt:
I'm trying to upgrade react-scripts from 4.x to 5.x in our Create React App project and npm is erroring out. Here's what I'm getting:

```
npm error code ERESOLVE
npm error ERESOLVE could not resolve
npm error
npm error While resolving: my-app@0.1.0
npm error Found: react@16.14.0
npm error node_modules/react
npm error   react@"^16.14.0" from the root project
npm error
npm error Could not resolve dependency:
npm error peer react@"^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0" from react-scripts@5.0.1
npm error node_modules/react-scripts
npm error   react-scripts@"5" from the root project
npm error
npm error Fix the upstream dependency conflict by installing
npm error with --legacy-peer-deps, or force resolve it with
npm error --force.
npm error
npm error Read more about it at:
npm error https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v9/using-npm/package-lock-json
```

I don't know if I should just add --legacy-peer-deps or if there's a real upgrade I need to do first. How do I figure out the full picture of what's blocking this and what are my options?
evals.expected_output: Should identify that react@16 is the root blocker — react-scripts@5 requires react@^17 or ^18. Should suggest using `npm explain react` to trace all constraints, and `npm view react-scripts@5 peerDependencies` to confirm what's required. Should present two paths: (1) upgrade react to v17 or v18 first, then install react-scripts@5, or (2) stay on react-scripts@4. Should explicitly advise against using --legacy-peer-deps long-term (it hides real conflicts). Should NOT jump straight to 'just run --force or --legacy-peer-deps' without explaining the underlying issue.

assertions.name: npm-explain-suggested
assertions.description: `npm explain` (or equivalent diagnostic command) is suggested to trace the dependency constraint

assertions.name: react-version-identified-as-root-blocker
assertions.description: react@16 being incompatible with react-scripts@5's peer dep requirement (^17 or ^18) is explicitly identified

assertions.name: multiple-options-presented
assertions.description: At least two paths are presented (e.g. upgrade react vs stay on react-scripts@4), not just one prescription

assertions.name: legacy-peer-deps-discouraged
assertions.description: --legacy-peer-deps is flagged as a short-term workaround to avoid long-term, not recommended as the solution

evals.prompt: I just merged main into my feature branch and now package-lock.json has a massive merge conflict. My branch added `zod` and `@trpc/server`, and main added `axios` and bumped a few existing packages. I don't want to just throw away one side — I need changes from both branches. What's the right approach?
evals.expected_output: Should explain that package-lock.json is auto-generated and conflict markers should never be edited by hand. Should direct the user to use `python3 scripts/diff_lock.py --conflict --format=summary` to see what changed on each side, then `python3 scripts/diff_lock.py --conflict` (without --format=summary) to get the exact npm install/uninstall commands. Should recommend running those commands to apply the other branch's changes precisely — NOT deleting the lock file and regenerating from scratch.

assertions.name: diff-lock-script-mentioned
assertions.description: `diff_lock.py` or `scripts/diff_lock.py` is mentioned as the tool to understand what changed on each side

assertions.name: lock-file-is-generated
assertions.description: Explains that package-lock.json is auto-generated and should not be manually edited to resolve conflicts

assertions.name: precise-npm-commands-used
assertions.description: Uses `diff_lock.py --conflict` output (specific npm install/uninstall commands) to apply the other branch's changes precisely, rather than deleting the lock file and regenerating from scratch

assertions.name: conflict-flag-used
assertions.description: The `--conflict` flag for diff_lock.py is shown, or the workflow describes using git to extract both sides for comparison

evals.prompt:
Haven't touched our dependencies in about 8 months. Just ran `npm outdated` on our Next.js production app. There's a lot here — where do I even start and what can I safely batch together?

```
Package                     Current   Wanted    Latest  Location
@types/node                 18.19.4   18.19.50  22.5.1  node_modules/@types/node
@types/react                18.2.48   18.3.3    18.3.3  node_modules/@types/react
axios                       1.6.5     1.7.7     1.7.7   node_modules/axios
date-fns                    2.30.0    2.30.0    4.1.0   node_modules/date-fns
eslint                      8.56.0    8.57.1    9.9.1   node_modules/eslint
next                        14.0.4    14.2.13   15.0.3  node_modules/next
react                       18.2.0    18.3.1    18.3.1  node_modules/react
react-dom                   18.2.0    18.3.1    18.3.1  node_modules/react-dom
tailwindcss                 3.4.1     3.4.13    3.4.13  node_modules/tailwindcss
zod                         3.22.4    3.23.8    3.23.8  node_modules/zod
```
evals.expected_output: Should triage by risk: patch/minor updates within current range (axios, @types/react, react, react-dom, tailwindcss, zod) are safe to batch with `npm update`; major bumps (date-fns 2→4, eslint 8→9, next 14→15, @types/node 18→22) each need individual handling. Should recommend running `npm audit` first to check for CVEs before starting. Should point out the Wanted vs Latest gap for @types/node and next (Wanted is still major-version old) — those need `npm install <pkg>@latest` not `npm update`. Should advise updating one major at a time with testing in between. Should NOT suggest running `npm update` with no package names on everything.

assertions.name: npm-audit-first
assertions.description: Recommends running `npm audit` as a first step before starting any upgrades

assertions.name: patch-minor-updates-batchable
assertions.description: Identifies patch/minor updates within the current range (e.g. axios, react, react-dom, tailwindcss, zod) as safe to batch together with `npm update`

assertions.name: major-updates-flagged-as-individual
assertions.description: Flags major version bumps (date-fns 2→4, eslint 8→9, next 14→15) as needing individual handling with testing between each

assertions.name: no-update-all-at-once
assertions.description: Does NOT suggest running `npm update` (no package names) to update everything at once

assertions.name: wanted-vs-latest-gap-explained
assertions.description: Notes that packages where Wanted is still old (e.g. next 14.x Wanted but 15.x Latest) require `npm install <pkg>@latest` rather than `npm update`

assertions.name: individual-branches-for-majors
assertions.description: Recommends doing each major version upgrade on its own branch (and/or commit) to isolate breakage
